purpose: Test whether growth/inflation direction and speed add stable out-of-sample information about Federal Reserve policy changes beyond macro levels.

conceptual_link_to_v66.interpretation: Issue #97 tests the economic premise behind direction/momentum information. It does not alter or directly fit V6.6.

timestamps.rationale: Two-month macro lag ensures IP/CPI observations are public before the policy forecast origin.
timestamps.current_policy_information: EFFR monthly average at m, known at month-end forecast origin.

features.missing_macro_policy: No interpolation; skip forecast origin if any required macro observation is unavailable.

primary_research_question: Does M2 add stable out-of-sample policy information over M1?

estimation.initial_training_end: 1969-12 forecast origins/outcomes available by that point
estimation.coefficient_information_rule: Each forecast is fit only on rows whose policy outcome is fully known before forecast month m.

directional: tighten/ease sign accuracy excluding neutral realized outcomes

decision_rules.direction_speed_adds_stable_policy_infor: M2 improves primary OOS error and directional metrics versus M1 with support across multiple eras and without one-era dependence.
decision_rules.levels_sufficient_no_incremental_speed_v: M2 adds no material/stable improvement over M1 while M1 itself has useful OOS policy information.
decision_rules.policy_relation_era_dependent: M2 or M1 has useful full-sample OOS information but incremental relationships materially reverse or disappear across major eras.
decision_rules.policy_model_unstable: All model variants show weak or unstable OOS policy information.
decision_rules.inconclusive_policy_evidence: Data gaps, small effective samples or conflicting diagnostics prevent a defensible classification.

stop_if: M2 does not add useful information and M1 is also weak/unstable
Any apparent M2 gain is isolated to one era

forbidden: Treasury-minus-cash outcome before Phase A finding
adding FCPI, real yield, term premium or market returns after failure
